A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SSR framework despite the changed title. Their text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable matching across renaming and relocation.

before.justification: v1 reports original nuScenes planning results, component and perception-task ablations, qualitative examples and latency measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds CARLA closed-loop evaluation, perception-pretraining experiments and navigation-command robustness results.

M1.justification: The original SSR procedure and losses remain unchanged; BEV World Model is renamed Future Feature Predictor. However, the added CARLA variant concatenates target points with navigation commands and uses a TCP planning head (Section 4.2), constituting a limited procedural adaptation.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates open-loop planning on nuScenes. v2 additionally trains on four CARLA towns and evaluates closed-loop driving on Town05 Long, substantially extending the environment and task requirements. Appendix E also adds systematic fixed and random navigation-command conditions.

E2.justification: The nuScenes comparator set in Table 1 is unchanged. New Table 2 introduces closed-loop comparisons with CILRS, LBC, Transfuser, Roach, TCP, ThinkTwice and DriveAdapter, alongside ST-P3 and VAD-Base, substantially broadening the comparison methods.

E3.justification: The original nuScenes protocol is retained. Sections 4.1–4.2 add disjoint-town CARLA evaluation using DS, RC and IS, with 189K training frames, ResNet-34, 900×256 images and 60 training epochs. Appendix E adds separate perception-pretraining and command-corruption protocols; these supplement rather than replace the original experiments.

E4.justification: Appendix E adds a control using weights pretrained for 48 epochs on perception tasks and quantitative robustness tests using constant or random navigation commands (Tables 7–8). These address the undertraining explanation and dependence on correct navigation inputs. The original ablations, qualitative failure cases and latency analysis are retained, sometimes relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, error bars or statistical significance tests. The new random-command experiment measures robustness rather than uncertainty across repeated runs.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the matched original ablation results retain their values. v2 adds CARLA results, including SSR driving score 78.9, and new appendix findings: perception pretraining gives average L2 error 1.11 versus 0.75 m, while constant-right commands give collision rate 0.53% versus 0.15% with original commands. Section 4.3 incorrectly states a 31.7-point advantage over TCP; Table 2 implies 21.7 points from 78.9 versus 57.2.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(16), including the token construction, prediction operations and losses, are unchanged. Neither version supplies theorems or proofs. The added standard CARLA metric descriptions do not introduce new mathematical reasoning or formal properties.

C1.justification: The performance contribution expands from state-of-the-art nuScenes planning to state-of-the-art open-loop and closed-loop performance. The abstract adds a 48.6-point Town05 Long driving-score advantage over VAD-Base. This substantially broadens the claimed empirical scope while retaining the central sparse-token, perception-supervision and efficiency claims.

C2.justification: Appendix E newly acknowledges that 12-epoch training may undertrain auxiliary perception branches and interprets the pretraining experiment as suggesting different scene understanding. It also discusses resilience and degradation under misleading commands, including conflicts with oncoming traffic under right-turn commands. These are focused extensions; the existing mechanism explanations and failure limitations remain.

D1.justification: Section 4.2 adds the 256-channel token dimension and a substantial CARLA implementation recipe, including backbone, image size, navigation inputs, planning head, hardware, batch size and learning-rate schedule. Appendix E specifies the perception-pretraining duration. The abstract also changes the code-access statement from a future release to reported availability.

R1.justification: v1's dedicated world-model related-work subsection is removed, together with references including GAIA-1, DriveWM and DriveWorld. v2 instead explicitly distinguishes direct feature supervision from Zong et al. (2023) and Zou et al. (2024), and introduces substantial CARLA and closed-loop literature. This changes the temporal component's positioning and broadens the comparison context.

P1.justification: v2 changes the title, publication header and module terminology, revises selected introductory passages, and distinguishes open-loop from closed-loop experiments. Appendix subsections A.1–A.4 become A–D, with the perception discussion moved into E. Most existing prose and the main narrative sequence remain closely matched.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 2, 7 and 8, splits v1 Table 2 into Tables 3–4, and relocates the perception ablation from Table 4 to appendix Table 6. Figures 2–4 receive color and label updates, and several existing figures move or gain clearer captions. The existing figure content and overall visual format are largely retained.

improvement.justification: v1's evaluation was limited to open-loop nuScenes planning. v2's documented CARLA adaptation adds evidence about driving with action feedback, while Appendix E tests the perception-undertraining explanation and quantifies sensitivity to misleading commands. These address important gaps in validation and substantially strengthen the paper. The new TCP comparison contains a localized arithmetic error, and uncertainty reporting remains absent, but these limitations do not outweigh the added substantive evidence.
